title: Scientific Reef Atlas
intent: Deliver a complete system for converting real reef surveys into trustworthy, explorable, versioned 3D sites.
outcome: A scientist can add a survey, inspect the reef at real scale, trace every object to its evidence, and compare site versions without using Isaac Sim or editing code.
deliverables: Survey intake for calibrated video, imagery, navigation, depth, sonar, and metadata
Repeatable photogrammetry and geometry-quality workflow
Georeferenced site catalog with immutable sources, licences, checksums, and uncertainty
OpenUSD visual, collision, analysis, and level-of-detail representations
Web and Isaac reef explorer with truth-class and provenance overlays
One complete 50 × 50 metre Red Sea reef district and documented operating runbook
acceptanceTests: A new authorized survey is processed from one manifest without manual scene editing
Scale, orientation, anchor, vertical datum, coverage, and reconstruction error pass documented tolerances
Every displayed reef asset resolves to source files, licence evidence, processing recipe, and checksums
The district streams and remains navigable at the agreed Mac and GPU performance targets
A clean machine can reproduce the published reef version and its validation report
gate: Release R1 only when Coral City operates as a usable scientific 3D reef atlas—not merely a rendered coral asset.

title: Ocean State and Forecast System
intent: Deliver historical, live, and forecast environmental state for each reef through one traceable model and observation system.
outcome: A scientist chooses a site and time and sees measured conditions, forecast conditions, uncertainty, data age, and model provenance as distinct layers.
deliverables: Spotter-compatible, weather, wave, ocean, and satellite connectors
Canonical Environment Package and independently testable model-adapter framework
Operational drift, wave, and coastal-field adapters selected from the model registry
NetCDF and Zarr field catalog with coordinate, unit, ensemble, and provenance enforcement
Historical replay, current conditions, forecast playback, and comparison dashboards
Scheduled ingestion, monitoring, retries, stale-data warnings, and forecast-skill reports
acceptanceTests: A thirty-day real-data period ingests and replays without missing provenance or truth classes
Identical model requests produce identical manifests and equivalent normalized fields
Observation, analysis, forecast, and scenario values cannot be confused in the interface or API
Connector and model failures appear as explicit operational states rather than silent gaps
Forecast output is compared with held-out observations using published skill metrics
gate: Release R2 only when it is a continuously operating environmental information product for a real site.

title: Underwater Robotics Laboratory
intent: Deliver a complete marine robotics simulator with a validated vehicle, sensors, operator experience, ROS 2, and environmental forcing.
outcome: An operator can drive or program an AUV through a real reef twin, inspect every sensor, record the mission, replay it, and receive an objective performance report.
deliverables: BlueROV-class six-degree-of-freedom vehicle, thrusters, buoyancy, drag, added mass, currents, and energy
Validated camera, IMU, depth, DVL, sonar, altimeter, CTD, timing, noise, and failure models
Keyboard and gamepad control plus chase, top, first-person, sonar, and science views
ROS 2 control, transforms, simulation time, software-in-the-loop, recording, and replay
Scenario runner, deterministic seeds, ground-truth isolation, and automated mission reports
Reference comparison against analytical cases, bench data, and a second marine simulator where useful
acceptanceTests: Station keeping, depth change, heading, straight-line motion, and energy cases pass tolerance envelopes
Every sensor passes rate, latency, frame, units, noise, dropout, and reference-value tests
The same ROS 2 mission runs live, records, replays, and produces the same scored outcome
Ground truth is unavailable to the robot but available to independent evaluation
A non-developer can launch, control, reset, and evaluate a mission from the operator interface
gate: Release R3 only when the simulator is a dependable robotics laboratory, not a manually driven visual demo.

title: Autonomy and Mission Certification
intent: Deliver repeatable autonomy development and pre-deployment certification across reef missions, conditions, and failures.
outcome: A team submits an autonomy stack and receives comparable evidence showing where it succeeds, fails, touches the reef, loses localization, or exhausts energy.
deliverables: Coverage, inspection, visual-sonar mapping, adaptive sampling, plume tracking, and return-home missions
Baseline localization, SLAM, perception, planning, control, and multi-vehicle implementations
Environmental ensembles, domain randomization, sensor faults, communications loss, and recovery cases
Batch simulation service, regression suite, mission scorecards, experiment registry, and result comparison
Software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop qualification profiles
Versioned mission certificate containing scope, limitations, evidence, and unresolved risks
acceptanceTests: Two autonomy stacks are compared on identical hidden scenario suites without changing the evaluator
Seeded runs are reproducible and ensemble runs report statistically meaningful confidence intervals
Reef contact, collision, localization, coverage, energy, safety, and scientific-value metrics are automatic
Known faults produce expected degraded behavior and never disappear from the final report
A release candidate passes a documented SIL and HIL profile before field approval
gate: Release R4 only when the laboratory can issue defensible, reproducible mission-readiness evidence.

title: Living Reef Intelligence System
intent: Deliver a time-aware ecological twin that explains observed reef change and directs the next useful observation.
outcome: A scientist can ask what changed, inspect the evidence and uncertainty, relate it to environmental exposure, and generate a targeted follow-up survey mission.
deliverables: Repeat-survey registration and structural change products with uncertainty
Coral, substrate, algae, damage, nursery, and intervention semantic layers
Colony and habitat histories linked to imagery, geometry, observations, and environmental exposure
Assimilated reef state, anomaly detection, review workflow, and versioned scientific annotations
Adaptive observation planner driven by uncertainty and ecological priority
Scientific reports and APIs that separate association, hypothesis, and validated inference
acceptanceTests: Known synthetic changes and independently reviewed real changes are detected within stated limits
Survey alignment error and biological-label uncertainty accompany every reported change
Every ecological claim resolves to observations, processing versions, reviewer state, and limitations
The system proposes a robot survey whose expected information gain can be measured after completion
A scientist can reproduce a published change report from preserved inputs
gate: Release R5 only when the twin supports a real repeat-survey scientific workflow from evidence to next observation.

title: Saudi Red Sea Field Operations
intent: Deliver the complete observe–predict–rehearse–deploy–learn loop at one partner-approved Saudi Red Sea site.
outcome: An operations team plans against current conditions, rehearses safely, deploys a real vehicle, monitors it, recovers its data, and updates the living twin.
deliverables: Partner-approved site, permissions, data governance, survey design, and safety case
Operational sensor feeds, forecasts, telemetry, alerts, health monitoring, and failure procedures
Mission planning, environmental go/no-go assessment, simulation rehearsal, and approval workflow
Live AUV tracking, operator timeline, event recording, and post-mission replay
Automated field-data intake, twin update, sim-to-real assessment, and model recalibration
Operational runbooks, training, support ownership, service objectives, and final pilot demonstration
acceptanceTests: A complete mission passes documented readiness, safety, data, and environmental checks
The field vehicle executes the rehearsed mission within approved operational bounds
Telemetry gaps, degraded sensors, aborts, and recovery actions are correctly recorded and surfaced
Real observations update the site and quantify simulator, sensor, and forecast error
A second trained operator can repeat the workflow from the maintained runbooks
gate: Release R6 only when one real site operates as a maintained field system and closes the learning loop.
